pages.lesson:
LESSON: PYTHAGOREAN RELATIONSHIP

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements
Topic 3.1: Pythagorean Relationship

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Pythagorean Relationship. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we use Pythagorean relationships in real-life situations?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise the sides of a right- angled triangle in different situations
2. identify Pythagorean relationships in different situations
3. apply Pythagorean relationship to real-life situations

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Pythagorean Relationship.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Pythagorean Relationship using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Do a variety of activities for example, counting squares on different sides of a 3, 4, 5 right angled-triangle, establish the Pythagorean relationship and practise using other right angled- triangles
2. Critical thinking and Problem-solving: as the learner identifies Pythagorean relationships in different situations such as a leaning ladder or staircase.
3. Creativity and Imagination: as the learner creates Pythagorean relationship puzzles.
4. Learning to Learn: as the learner applies Pythagorean relationships in real-life situations. Values
5. Unity: as the learner carries out various activities together, such as creating Pythagorean relationship puzzles.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Pythagorean Relationship is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
